mission: The land gets a brain and hands of its own, run by the people who live there.

areas.name: Sensing
areas.summary: The node’s eyes and ears. Today’s best forest nodes listen and alert. They do not own a plot.

areas.name: Machines
areas.summary: Autonomy is already real in mines, solar trenching, and some construction. Ecological restoration earthworks with a friendly construction look are mostly open. This branch waits on the node, the record, the relationships, and the safety stack.

areas.name: Security
areas.summary: Safety is designed in from day one, because the long-term plan includes machines. This map covers the what and why, not a build guide, a wiring diagram, or a parts list.

areas.name: Data and intelligence
areas.summary: Local records, a design engine that learns from healthy land, and drafts a qualified person still signs.

areas.name: Governance
areas.summary: The people who live there own the node and the record, and they approve large changes.

areas.name: Jobs and people
areas.summary: The point is more paid human work, not less. The node helps describe work; trained local people do it.

areas.name: Power and energy
areas.summary: Solar power for the first box, and later a quiet machine drive compatible with a physical stop.

areas.name: Biology and mycelium
areas.summary: A later research branch. Stay honest about the debate. It is not part of the first node, and it is not part of the mid-game monitoring offer.

nodes.name: Off-grid soil and microclimate suite
nodes.stageNote: A node that also designs the plot and commands machines is later, and still research.
nodes.statusNote: Buildable now for the first box.
nodes.summary: A rugged solar plot node that stores the record locally, later runs the plot’s artificial intelligence (AI), and later commands machines on a private network, with no required cloud. The first box is simpler: a weatherproof enclosure, solar power and storage, a single-board computer, local storage, and a few honest sensors for temperature, soil moisture, and plot microclimate, plus the hydrology in LR01.2. The historic record (LR04.3) starts the day this box is switched on.
nodes.uncertainty: Whether year-one hardware can stay up through a full season without a cloud must be measured, not guessed. Wetland-specific edge AI is still early.

nodes.name: Dead-man’s link

nodes.summary: Power stays on only while a signed local heartbeat says OK. Lose it, and the loop drops. For large earthworks, a person who approved the job is part of that OK. A remote cloud cannot keep the machine alive. Jammed radio, a dead node, or a cut cable must drop the loop.

nodes.name: Plot-owned, decades-to-centuries record that drives next year’s work
nodes.stageNote: Early to start an honest local record. Late as a decades-scale operational brain.
nodes.statusNote: Buildable now to start the record. National research archives exist and remain the teachers.
nodes.summary: Durable local storage, open formats, checksums, one-way copies off site, and physical samples when it matters. The record belongs to the people of that place, including people not born yet, and it actually retunes design and machine work. Start the record the day the first node is switched on. Do not invent how valuable an old node will be; the claim is directional, from long-running research records.
nodes.uncertainty: Those archives are research infrastructures, not a private plot’s operational brain.

nodes.name: Cheap field soil probes for carbon-13, biodegradable dye, or a DNA barcode

nodes.name: Arrival-time visualization (hours to days, as a time-lapse)
nodes.statusNote: Research. No field-ready product was found.
nodes.summary: Software that turns probe arrivals, and later electrical or chemical changes if the methods hold up, into a glowing map. Spread will take hours to days, not milliseconds. The map can only show what the probes actually detect. It must not be presented as proof of a tree internet.

dryad.label: Dryad Silvanet
dryad.note: Commercial solar, supercapacitor wildfire and microclimate sensor. Long maintenance-free life is a company claim.

sparrow.label: Microsoft SPARROW
sparrow.note: Open-source solar edge-AI (artificial intelligence) research platform on an NVIDIA Jetson. Field-deployment descriptions are a vendor claim. Not a turnkey wetland product.

treetalker.label: Nature 4.0 TreeTalker Cyber
treetalker.note: Tree-physiology node. Often a battery device; do not assume it is off-grid solar.

kerala.label: Kerala Ramsar edge-AI preprint (2025–2026)
kerala.note: Preprint describing solar single-board computers at a Ramsar site. Not a peer-reviewed product.

solinst.label: Solinst Levelogger ecohydrology note
solinst.note: Water-level loggers documented in ecohydrological research.

aquatroll.label: In-Situ Aqua TROLL 700
aquatroll.note: Commercial multiparameter sonde. Product details on the maker’s page are a vendor claim. Optional telemetry should not be the default for an offline-first node.

swmp.label: NOAA System-Wide Monitoring Program
swmp.note: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) water-quality and weather measurements every 15 minutes across the 30 National Estuarine Research Reserves.

nerrsdata.label: NOAA NERRS SWMP data portal
nerrsdata.note: Data portal for the reserve monitoring program.

cfr122.label: 40 CFR 122.48
cfr122.note: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) rules can require continuous monitoring.

maine.label: Maine DEP continuous monitoring SOP (2023)
maine.note: State standard operating procedure treating unattended sonde data as usable when calibration procedures are followed.

wrap.label: U.S. Army Corps ERDC TN-WRAP-05-2
wrap.note: Technical standard recommending automated water-table recorders as hydrology evidence, with verification against manual readings.

cfr3326.label: 33 CFR 332.6
cfr3326.note: Federal wetland mitigation rule: a monitoring period of not less than five years.

cfr3327.label: 33 CFR 332.7
cfr3327.note: Federal wetland mitigation rule: adaptive management when monitoring shows a project is not meeting its targets.

ser.label: SER International Standards, 2nd edition (2019)
ser.note: Society for Ecological Restoration (SER) standards tell practitioners to build restoration targets from reference models based on real, less-damaged sites.

swamp.label: CNR–INM SWAMP vessel review
swamp.note: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche – Institute of Marine Engineering (CNR–INM) research uncrewed surface vehicle for ultra-shallow wetlands.

medusa.label: MEDUSA (Frontiers in Environmental Science, 2022)
medusa.note: Aerial-aquatic research prototype with a tethered micro-uncrewed underwater vehicle, validated for chlorophyll-a profiling.

bluerov.label: Blue Robotics BlueROV2
bluerov.note: Established general inspection remotely operated vehicle, not a wetland-specific explorer.

restor.label: Restor
restor.note: Maps and reports restoration sites. It does not output earthwork plans or drive machines. About-page site counts from the research pass are not repeated here.

restor_about.label: Restor about page
restor_about.note: Project about page for Restor (Crowther Lab spin-off).

bioprime.label: NIOZ BIOPRIME
bioprime.note: Research project, 1 August 2025–30 September 2031, on biodegradable structures that mimic habitat-forming traits. Structures, not algorithms running machines.

flash.label: Flash Forest
flash.note: Commercial reforestation company. Descriptions of light detection and ranging (LiDAR) and machine-learning forest intelligence are company claims.

mast.label: Mast Reforestation
mast.note: Commercial reforestation company (aerial work, nurseries, site work).

built.label: Built Robotics Exosystem
built.note: Aftermarket kit that turns mid-size excavators into autonomous trenchers, with geofencing and a wireless emergency stop. Accuracy figures are company specs. Trenching, not wetland restoration.

komatsu.label: Komatsu / EARTHBRAIN / AIM release (31 July 2026)
komatsu.note: Company release saying autonomous dozers and excavators are in commercial U.S. deployment and can be retrofitted.

cat.label: Caterpillar autonomy release (7 January 2026)
cat.note: Company release describing mature mining autonomy and an announced “next era” of construction autonomy. That is not a claim that crewless excavators are already standard on ordinary jobsites. Company fleet figures are not repeated here.

autoplant.label: SCA Autoplant
autoplant.note: Sweden’s Autoplant project ended 11 September 2026 with a working scarify-and-plant head, still pulled by a conventional forwarder.

doi_am.label: U.S. Department of the Interior Adaptive Management Technical Guide (2009)
doi_am.note: Describes a cycle of objectives, action, monitoring, assessment, and adjustment.

parkgrass.label: Rothamsted Park Grass experiment
parkgrass.note: Began in 1856 and is still running.

parkgrass_news.label: Rothamsted 170-year note
parkgrass_news.note: The research institute calls Park Grass the world’s longest-running grassland experiment. That wording is the institute’s own.

lter.label: U.S. LTER Network about page
lter.note: Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) Network, founded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) in 1980. The about page, updated 16 March 2026, reports 26 sites and more than 45 years of public observations.

neon.label: National Ecological Observatory Network
neon.note: 81 field sites; construction finished May 2019; public data portal. Operated by Battelle, funded by NSF.

neon_faq.label: NEON FAQ
neon_faq.note: Official FAQ for the observatory network.

sitemarker.label: SiteMarker
sitemarker.note: Geo-referenced, permit-oriented reports from a site walk.

ecobot.label: Ecobot monitoring
ecobot.note: Used for wetland permitting. A monitoring product in private beta can pull logger hydrology and draft regulator-template reports, with a person still in the loop.

safecast.label: Safecast
safecast.note: Volunteer radiation and later air-quality data published into the public domain under a Creative Commons Zero (CC0) dedication. Does not control machines.

sensorcom.label: Sensor.Community
sensorcom.note: Civic-tech network with open hardware, software, and data. Does not control machines.

crowdsorsa.label: Crowdsorsa
crowdsorsa.note: Pays for environmental microtasks, including invasive-plant removal, with quality control before payment.

earthoptics.label: EarthOptics FieldTech
earthoptics.note: On-demand agricultural soil sampling, not wetland naturalist work.

owl.label: Owl Cyber Defense data diodes
owl.note: Industrial data diode product line. Use of data diodes in industrial plants is field-proven as a class of control, not as a solar plot-node product.

gza.label: GZA on data diodes in water utilities
gza.note: Write-up on data diodes in water infrastructure, including Fend.

story.label: Peter Story, 2023 SOUPS paper
story.note: Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security (SOUPS) paper describing a commodity-fiber diode built as a research demonstration. Cost figures in that paper are from 2023, are not a current quote, and are not published here.

osdd.label: Open Source Data Diode notes
osdd.note: Open hardware notes for a data diode.

adamatzky.label: Adamatzky, 2022, Royal Society Open Science
adamatzky.note: Laboratory recordings of electrical spike patterns in mycelium. A page fetch timed out on one research pass; the 2022 Royal Society record is the citation used here.

adamatzky_pmc.note: PubMed Central copy of the 2022 laboratory study.

buffi_pmc.note: PubMed Central copy of the 2025 review.
